title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No mathematical errors. Counts check out: |M^*| = 12, |Δ| = 6, C(6,2) = 15, 15 − 3 = 12 edges, 2^3 = 8 faces.
Minor slip on the next page: 'parties de I' should read 'parties de J', consistent with this page.

ideas.what: P^1(Z/4Z) as M^*/{±1}, fibred 2:1 over P^1(F_2) by reduction, with M^* → J a torsor under the constant group M_0
ideas.modern_name: Projective line over Z/4; reduction map P^1(Z/p^2) → P^1(F_p); cusps of Γ(4)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Fricke) for the cusps of X(4); standard in modular-curve theory

ideas.what: Intrinsic octahedron structure on P^1(Z/4): diagonals = fibres over P^1(F_2), faces = sections, edges = partial sections over 2-element subsets
ideas.modern_name: Octahedral configuration of the 6 cusps of X(4) (Klein's octahedral covering)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Klein (octahedral modular curve X(4)); the fibrewise/sections phrasing is a reformulation
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Platonic solids/dessins and modular curves in general terms, but not this specific construction

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, choice-free (canonical) description of the classical octahedral structure on the level-4 cusps, P^1(Z/4), via sections of the reduction map. It is elegant in Grothendieck's style but mathematically classical and routine.
transcription_corrections: 'ce sont les points w.r.t. dans Λ·Z/4Z' likely reads 'ce sont les points à val. dans Λ = Z/4Z' (points with values in Z/4Z).
'M^*_*' in 'opère sur M^*_*' is just M^*.
'la structure de [l'ens. des sommets] d'un octaèdre' is correct as an inserted bracket: Δ is the vertex set of an octahedron, J the set of diagonals.
